        .stc-club-card-content {
            padding: 40px 28px;
            display: flex;
            flex-direction: column;
            align-items: center;
            flex: 1;
        }

        .stc-club-card img {
            width: 120px;
            height: 120px;
            border-radius: 50%;
            margin-bottom: 24px;
            object-fit: cover;
            border: 3px solid var(--border-light);
            transition: all 0.3s ease;
            flex-shrink: 0;
            background: var(--bg-light);
        }

        .stc-club-card img[src*=".png"],
        .stc-club-card img[src*=".jpg"],
        .stc-club-card img[src*=".jpeg"] {
            object-fit: contain;
            padding: 8px;
        }

        .stc-club-card:hover img {
            transform: scale(1.1);
            border-color: var(--primary-color);
        }

        .stc-club-card h3 {
            font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif;
            font-size: 1.4rem;
            font-weight: 600;
            color: var(--text-primary);
            margin-bottom: 16px;
            flex-shrink: 0;
        }

        .stc-club-card p {
            color: var(--text-secondary);
            font-size: 1rem;
            line-height: 1.6;
            flex: 1;
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            margin-bottom: 20px;
            text-align: center;
        }

        .club-contact {
            margin-top: auto;
            padding-top: 16px;
            border-top: 1px solid var(--border-light);
            width: 100%;
        }

        .club-contact small {
            color: var(--text-secondary);
            font-size: 0.8rem;
            display: block;
            text-align: center;
            opacity: 0.8;
        }

        /* Sliding Gallery */
        .gallery-container {
            position: relative;
            overflow: hidden;
            border-radius: 20px;
            margin: 3rem 0;
        }

        .gallery-slider {
            display: flex;
            transition: transform 0.5s ease;
        }

        .gallery-slide {
            min-width: 100%;
            position: relative;
        }

        .gallery-slide img {
            width: 100%;
            height: 500px;
            object-fit: cover;
            border-radius: 20px;
            transition: opacity 0.3s ease;
        }

        .gallery-slide img[loading="lazy"] {
            opacity: 0;
        }

        .gallery-slide img.loaded {
            opacity: 1;
        }

        .gallery-caption {
            position: absolute;
            bottom: 0;
            left: 0;
            right: 0;
            background: linear-gradient(transparent, rgba(0,0,0,0.8));
            color: white;
            padding: 2rem 2rem 1.5rem;
            border-bottom-left-radius: 20px;
            border-bottom-right-radius: 20px;
            transform: translateY(100%);
            transition: transform 0.3s ease;
        }

        .gallery-slide:hover .gallery-caption {
            transform: translateY(0);
        }

        .gallery-caption h4 {
            margin: 0 0 0.5rem 0;
            font-size: 1.25rem;
            font-weight: 600;
            font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif;
        }

        .gallery-caption p {
            margin: 0;
            font-size: 0.875rem;
            opacity: 0.9;
            line-height: 1.4;
        }

        .gallery-controls {
            position: absolute;
            top: 50%;
            transform: translateY(-50%);
            width: 100%;
            display: flex;
            justify-content: space-between;
            padding: 0 20px;
            pointer-events: none;
        }

        .gallery-btn {
            background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.95);
            color: var(--primary-color);
            border: none;
            width: 50px;
            height: 50px;
            border-radius: 50%;
            cursor: pointer;
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            justify-content: center;
            font-size: 1.5rem;
            transition: all 0.3s ease;
            pointer-events: all;
            box-shadow: var(--shadow-lg);
        }

        .gallery-btn:hover {
            background: white;
            transform: scale(1.1);
            color: var(--primary-dark);
        }

        .gallery-dots {
            position: absolute;
            bottom: 20px;
            left: 50%;
            transform: translateX(-50%);
            display: flex;
            gap: 10px;
        }

        .dot {
            width: 12px;
            height: 12px;
            border-radius: 50%;
            background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5);
            cursor: pointer;
            transition: all 0.3s ease;
        }

        .dot.active {
            background: var(--primary-color);
            transform: scale(1.3);
        }

        /* Events Timeline */
        .stc-events-grid {
            display: grid;
            grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(320px, 1fr));
            gap: 24px;
            margin-top: 3rem;
        }

        .stc-event-card {
            background: white;
            border-radius: 12px;
            padding: 24px;
            box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.1), 0 2px 4px -1px rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.06);
            border-left: 4px solid var(--primary-color);
            transition: all 0.3s ease;
            display: flex;
            flex-direction: column;
            height: 200px;
        }

        .stc-event-card:hover {
            transform: translateY(-4px);
            box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.1), 0 4px 6px -2px rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.05);
        }

        .stc-event-date {
            color: var(--primary-color);
            font-weight: 600;
            font-size: 0.875rem;
            margin-bottom: 12px;
            flex-shrink: 0;
        }

        .stc-event-card h3 {
            color: var(--text-primary);
            margin-bottom: 12px;
            font-size: 1.125rem;
            font-weight: 600;
            line-height: 1.4;
            flex-shrink: 0;
        }

        .stc-event-card p {
            color: var(--text-secondary);
            font-size: 0.875rem;
            line-height: 1.5;
            flex: 1;
        }

        .stc-event-cta {
            margin-top: 16px;
            padding: 8px 16px;
            background: var(--primary-color);
            color: white;
            border: none;
            border-radius: 6px;
            font-size: 0.875rem;
            font-weight: 500;
            cursor: pointer;
            transition: background-color 0.2s ease;
            text-decoration: none;
            display: inline-block;
            text-align: center;
            flex-shrink: 0;
        }

        .stc-event-cta:hover {
            background: var(--primary-dark);
            color: white;
            text-decoration: none;
        }

        /* Updates Grid */
        .updates-grid {
            display: grid;
            grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(350px, 1fr));
            gap: 30px;
            margin-top: 3rem;
        }

        .update-card {
            background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--bg-white), var(--bg-light));
            border-radius: 15px;
            padding: 25px;
            box-shadow: var(--shadow-md);
            transition: all 0.3s ease;
        }

        .update-card:hover {
            transform: translateY(-5px);
            box-shadow: var(--shadow-lg);
        }

        .update-meta {
            display: flex;
            justify-content: space-between;
            margin-bottom: 15px;
            font-size: 0.85rem;
            color: var(--text-secondary);
        }

        .update-card h3 {
            color: var(--text-primary);
            margin-bottom: 10px;
            font-size: 1.25rem;
        }

        .update-card p {
            color: var(--text-secondary);
            line-height: 1.6;
        }

        /* Fade in animation */
        .fade-in-section {
            opacity: 0;
            transform: translateY(30px);
            transition: all 0.8s ease;
        }

        .fade-in-section.visible {
            opacity: 1;
            transform: translateY(0);
        }

        /* Responsive Design */
        @media (max-width: 992px) {
            .stc-clubs-grid {
                grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(240px, 1fr));
                gap: 20px;
            }

            .stc-events-grid {
                grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr));
            }

            .stc-highlights-grid {
                grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr));
                gap: 20px;
            }

            .gallery-slide img {
                height: 400px;
            }
        }

        @media (max-width: 768px) {
            #hero h1 {
                font-size: 2.5rem;
            }

            .hero-tagline {
                font-size: 1.1rem;
                margin-bottom: 2.5rem;
            }

            .hero-ctas {
                flex-direction: column;
                align-items: center;
                gap: 16px;
            }

            .hero-btn-primary,
            .hero-btn-secondary {
                padding: 16px 32px;
                font-size: 1rem;
                width: 100%;
                max-width: 280px;
            }

            .hero-highlights {
                grid-template-columns: 1fr;
                gap: 16px;
                margin-top: 2rem;
            }

            #featured-clubs {
                padding: 100px 0 80px 0;
                margin-top: 30px;
            }

            .section-title {
                font-size: 2rem;
            }

            .stc-clubs-grid {
                grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
                gap: 20px;
                padding: 0 10px;
            }

            .stc-club-card {
                height: 380px;
            }

            .stc-club-card-content {
                padding: 28px 20px;
            }

            .stc-club-card img {
                width: 100px;
                height: 100px;
                margin-bottom: 20px;
            }

            .stc-club-card h3 {
                font-size: 1.2rem;
                margin-bottom: 12px;
            }

            .stc-club-card p {
                font-size: 0.9rem;
                line-height: 1.5;
            }

            .club-contact small {
                font-size: 0.75rem;
            }

            .stc-events-grid {
                grid-template-columns: 1fr;
                gap: 16px;
            }

            .stc-event-card {
                height: auto;
                min-height: 160px;
            }

            .gallery-slide img {
                height: 300px;
            }
        }

        @media (max-width: 480px) {
            #hero h1 {
                font-size: 2rem;
            }

            .hero-tagline {
                font-size: 1rem;
            }

            .hero-btn-primary,
            .hero-btn-secondary {
                padding: 14px 28px;
                font-size: 0.95rem;
            }

            #featured-clubs {
                padding: 80px 0 70px 0;
                margin-top: 20px;
            }

            .stc-clubs-grid {
                grid-template-columns: 1fr;
                gap: 24px;
                padding: 0 5px;
            }

            .stc-club-card {
                height: 400px;
                margin: 0 auto;
                max-width: 350px;
            }

            .stc-club-card-content {
                padding: 32px 24px;
            }

            .stc-club-card img {
                width: 110px;
                height: 110px;
                margin-bottom: 20px;
            }

            .gallery-slide img {
                height: 250px;
            }
        }

        /* Accessibility */
        .sr-only {
            position: absolute;
            width: 1px;
            height: 1px;
            padding: 0;
            margin: -1px;
            overflow: hidden;
            clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0);
            white-space: nowrap;
            border: 0;
        }

        /* Focus styles */
        a:focus,
        button:focus {
            outline: 2px solid var(--primary-color);
            outline-offset: 2px;
        }

        /* Loading animation */
        .skeleton {
            background: linear-gradient(90deg, #f0f0f0 25%, #e0e0e0 50%, #f0f0f0 75%);
            background-size: 200% 100%;
            animation: loading 1.5s infinite;
        }

        @keyframes loading {
            0% { background-position: 200% 0; }
            100% { background-position: -200% 0; }
        }
    </style>
</head>

    <script src="js/script.js"></script>
    
    <!-- Enhanced JavaScript for new features -->
    <script>
        // Hero Background Image Rotation
        const heroBackgroundImages = [
            'images/gallery/Events/Anvesha/Inauguration/_AAR6973 (1).JPG',
            'images/gallery/Events/Anvesha/Afficionados/_AAR7137.JPG',
            'images/gallery/Events/Crucible/opticsboard.jpeg',
            'images/gallery/Events/National Science Day/_AJN4997 (1).JPG',
            'images/gallery/Events/Panel Discussion/IMG-20250615-PANELISTS.jpg',
            'images/gallery/Events/Anvesha/BahFest/_OMJ8296 (1).JPG',
            'images/gallery/Events/Anvesha/Blender Workshop/_ESV4906.JPG'
        ];
        
        let currentHeroImageIndex = 0;
        
        function rotateHeroBackground() {
            const hero = document.getElementById('hero');
            if (hero) {
                currentHeroImageIndex = (currentHeroImageIndex + 1) % heroBackgroundImages.length;
                hero.style.setProperty('--hero-bg-image', `url('${heroBackgroundImages[currentHeroImageIndex]}')`);
            }
        }
        
        // Start hero background rotation
        setInterval(rotateHeroBackground, 8000); // Change every 8 seconds
        
        // Gallery Slider Functionality
        const slider = document.getElementById('gallerySlider');
        const slides = slider.querySelectorAll('.gallery-slide');
        const prevBtn = document.getElementById('prevBtn');
        const nextBtn = document.getElementById('nextBtn');
        const dotsContainer = document.getElementById('galleryDots');
        
        let currentSlide = 0;
        const totalSlides = slides.length;
        
        // Create dots
        for (let i = 0; i < totalSlides; i++) {
            const dot = document.createElement('span');
            dot.classList.add('dot');
            if (i === 0) dot.classList.add('active');
            dot.addEventListener('click', () => goToSlide(i));
            dotsContainer.appendChild(dot);
        }
        
        const dots = dotsContainer.querySelectorAll('.dot');
        
        function updateSlider() {
            slider.style.transform = `translateX(-${currentSlide * 100}%)`;
            
            dots.forEach((dot, index) => {
                dot.classList.toggle('active', index === currentSlide);
            });
        }
        
        function goToSlide(slideIndex) {
            currentSlide = slideIndex;
            updateSlider();
        }
        
        function nextSlide() {
            currentSlide = (currentSlide + 1) % totalSlides;
            updateSlider();
        }
        
        function prevSlide() {
            currentSlide = (currentSlide - 1 + totalSlides) % totalSlides;
            updateSlider();
        }
        
        prevBtn.addEventListener('click', prevSlide);
        nextBtn.addEventListener('click', nextSlide);
        
        // Auto-play functionality
        let autoPlayInterval;
        
        function startAutoPlay() {
            autoPlayInterval = setInterval(nextSlide, 5000); // Change slide every 5 seconds
        }
        
        function stopAutoPlay() {
            clearInterval(autoPlayInterval);
        }
        
        // Start auto-play when page loads
        startAutoPlay();
        
        // Pause auto-play when user hovers over gallery
        const galleryContainer = document.querySelector('.gallery-container');
        if (galleryContainer) {
            galleryContainer.addEventListener('mouseenter', stopAutoPlay);
            galleryContainer.addEventListener('mouseleave', startAutoPlay);
        }
        
        // Pause auto-play when user interacts with controls
        prevBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
            stopAutoPlay();
            setTimeout(startAutoPlay, 3000); // Restart after 3 seconds
        });
        
        nextBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
            stopAutoPlay();
            setTimeout(startAutoPlay, 3000); // Restart after 3 seconds
        });
        
        dots.forEach(dot => {
            dot.addEventListener('click', () => {
                stopAutoPlay();
                setTimeout(startAutoPlay, 3000); // Restart after 3 seconds
            });
        });
        
        // Keyboard navigation
        document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
            if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft') prevSlide();
            if (e.key === 'ArrowRight') nextSlide();
        });
        
        // Touch/Swipe support for mobile
        let touchStartX = 0;
        let touchEndX = 0;
        
        if (galleryContainer) {
            galleryContainer.addEventListener('touchstart', (e) => {
                touchStartX = e.changedTouches[0].screenX;
            });
            
            galleryContainer.addEventListener('touchend', (e) => {
                touchEndX = e.changedTouches[0].screenX;
                handleSwipe();
            });
        }
        
        function handleSwipe() {
            if (touchEndX < touchStartX - 50) nextSlide();
            if (touchEndX > touchStartX + 50) prevSlide();
        }
        
        // Intersection Observer for fade-in animations
        const observerOptions = {
            threshold: 0.1,
            rootMargin: '0px 0px -50px 0px'
        };
        
        const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
            entries.forEach(entry => {
                if (entry.isIntersecting) {
                    entry.target.classList.add('visible');
                }
            });
        }, observerOptions);
        
        // Observe all sections with fade-in-section class
        document.querySelectorAll('.fade-in-section').forEach(section => {
            observer.observe(section);
        });
        
        // Smooth scroll for anchor links
        document.querySelectorAll('a[href^="#"]').forEach(anchor => {
            anchor.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
                e.preventDefault();
                const target = document.querySelector(this.getAttribute('href'));
                if (target) {
                    target.scrollIntoView({
                        behavior: 'smooth',
                        block: 'start'
                    });
                }
            });
        });
        
        // Sample data for events and updates (replace with actual data from data.js)

                        </a>

        }
        
        function loadSampleUpdates() {
            const updatesContainer = document.getElementById('latest-updates-grid');
            const sampleUpdates = [

        // Load sample data on page load
        document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {

            // Preload gallery images for faster loading
            const preloadGalleryImages = () => {
                const galleryImages = [
                    'images/gallery/Events/Anvesha/Inauguration/direc.JPG',

            // Add fast loading for images with fade-in effect

                const imageLoad = () => {
                    img.style.opacity = '1';
                };
                
                if (img.complete) {

                } else {

                    img.addEventListener('error', () => {
                        img.style.opacity = '0.5';
                        console.warn('Failed to load image:', img.src);

                }
            });
            
            // Start preloading after page load

        // Performance optimization: Enhanced lazy loading with fast intersection detection

                entries.forEach(entry => {
                    if (entry.isIntersecting) {

                        const src = img.dataset.src || img.src;
                        
                        // Create a new image for faster loading

                            img.src = src;

                            img.style.opacity = '1';
                        };

                        observer.unobserve(img);
                    }
                });

Here’s a breakdown of the issues and how to fix them. 1. Hero Section Background Image The initial background image for your hero section is set using a Google Drive link, which won't work. The Problem: The URL you've used in your CSS is a link to a Google Drive viewing page, not a direct link to the image file itself. Browsers cannot render a webpage as a background image. #hero {
    /* ... */
    --hero-bg-image: url('https://drive.google.com/file/d/1szoSfa31OAJy5SFjUxw8hhYt3QyMvSuS/view'); /* Incorrect URL */
} The Fix: Replace this URL with a correct relative path to one of the images you use in your JavaScript rotator. Since the rotator will change it anyway, this just provides a valid starting image. /* Corrected CSS */
#hero {
    /* ... */
    --hero-bg-image: url('images/gallery/Events/Anvesha/Inauguration/_AAR6973 (1).JPG');
} 2. Gallery Images & Rotating Hero Background All other images in your gallery and the JavaScript hero background rotator use relative paths (e.g., images/gallery/... ). If these are not loading, it means your folder structure is incorrect. The Problem: The browser is looking for a folder named images in the same directory as your HTML file. If it can't find the images there, they will appear broken. The Fix: Ensure your project's folder structure is set up correctly. Your main HTML file should be in the root folder, alongside the images , css , and js folders. Verify your folder structure looks like this: your-project-folder/
├── index.html         <-- Your main HTML file
├── images/            <-- Folder containing all your images
│   └── gallery/
│       └── ...
├── css/
│   └── style.css
└── js/
    └── script.js Also, double-check for any typos , extra spaces, or case-sensitivity issues in your file paths and names. For example, image.JPG is different from image.jpg on some web servers. These styles use media queries to adjust the layout for different screen sizes, ensuring a good user experience on desktops, tablets, and mobile phones. The key changes involve: Making grid layouts stack into single or double columns on smaller screens. Adjusting font sizes and padding for better readability on mobile devices. Ensuring images and content blocks scale properly. Here is your HTML with the necessary responsive CSS added inside a <style> tag in the <head> section. You can copy this code directly or add the CSS rules to your existing css/style.css file. <!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">

    <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/style.css">

    <style>
        /* This is a placeholder for your existing styles. 
        The responsive styles below will build upon them.
        For example, your original CSS might look something like this:
        
        .container {
            width: 90%;
            max-width: 1200px;
            margin: 0 auto;
            padding: 0 20px;
        }
        .clubs-grid {
            display: grid;
            grid-template-columns: repeat(5, 1fr);
            gap: 20px;
        }
        .gallery-grid {
            display: grid;
            grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
        }
        #hero h1 {
            font-size: 3em;
        }
        */

        /* --- Responsive Styles --- */

        /* For Tablets and smaller devices (max-width: 992px) */
        @media (max-width: 992px) {
            .clubs-grid {
                /* Allows 3 or 4 clubs per row on tablets */
                grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr));
            }

            .gallery-grid {
                /* Shows 2 images per row */
                grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
            }
        }

        /* For smaller tablets and mobile phones (max-width: 768px) */
        @media (max-width: 768px) {
            .container {
                /* Reduces side padding on smaller screens */
                padding-left: 15px;
                padding-right: 15px;
            }

            #hero h1 {
                /* Reduces heading size for readability */
                font-size: 2.2em;
                line-height: 1.2;
            }
            
            #hero .tagline {
                font-size: 1.1em;
            }

            .section-title {
                font-size: 1.8em;
            }

            .clubs-grid {
                /* Shows 2 clubs per row */
                grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
                gap: 15px;
            }
            
            .updates-grid, .events-timeline {
                /* Stacks updates and events vertically */
                grid-template-columns: 1fr;
            }

            .gallery-grid {
                /* Ensures gallery items don't get too small */
                grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr));
            }
        }

        /* For small mobile phones (max-width: 480px) */
        @media (max-width: 480px) {
            #hero h1 {
                /* Further reduces heading size */
                font-size: 1.8em;
            }

            #hero .tagline {
                font-size: 1em;
            }

            .clubs-grid {
                /* Stacks club cards into a single column */
                grid-template-columns: 1fr;
            }
            
            .gallery-grid {
                /* Stacks gallery images into a single column */
                grid-template-columns: 1fr;
            }

            .cta-button {
                /* Makes button slightly smaller */
                padding: 12px 20px;
                font-size: 0.9em;
            }
        }
    </style>
</head>

### Interaction 917
Gemini Apps Created Gemini Canvas titled Website Blueprint for STC IISER TVM # Website Blueprint: Science and Technology Council (STC), IISER Thiruvananthapuram

## 1. Vision & Strategy

**Objective:** To create a modern, clean, and engaging website that serves as the central hub for the Science and Technology Council (STC) of IISER Thiruvananthapuram. The site will provide comprehensive information about the STC, its clubs, events, and members, while reflecting a professional and innovative image.

**Target Audience:**

* Current and prospective students of IISER TVM

* Faculty and administration

* Participants and attendees of STC events (e.g., Anvesha)

* General public interested in science and technology activities at IISER TVM

**Design Philosophy:**

* **Modern & Clean:** Inspired by the minimalist and elegant design of Apple's website.

* **User-Centric:** Intuitive navigation and a seamless user experience (UX/UI).

* **Visually Driven:** High-quality images, logos, and a sophisticated color palette.

* **Responsive:** Optimized for all devices (desktops, tablets, and smartphones).

**Color Palette:**

* **Primary:** Violet (e.g., `#6A0DAD` or a similar modern shade)

* **Secondary:** White (e.g., `#FFFFFF`)

* **Accent:** Light Gray (e.g., `#F5F5F7`) for backgrounds and subtle contrasts.

* **Text:** Dark Gray/Black (e.g., `#1D1D1F`) for readability.

## 2. Website Structure & Pages

### **Homepage**

* **Hero Section:** A full-screen, high-resolution image or a subtle video background showcasing a recent event or campus life.

  * **Headline:** "Science and Technology Council, IISER Thiruvananthapuram"

  * **Tagline:** "Fostering Innovation, Inspiring Minds."

  * **Call-to-Action (CTA) Button:** "Explore Our Clubs" or "Latest Events"

* **Featured Clubs:** A visually appealing grid or carousel with the logos and names of prominent clubs (CCIT, CMIT, Parsec, psit, proteus.) with their detals . Clicking on a logo will navigate to the respective club's page.

* **Upcoming Events:** A clean, timeline-style section highlighting the next 2-3 major events, including Anvesha. Each event should have a brief description, date, and a "Learn More" link.

* **Latest Updates:** A section with the three most recent announcements or news articles.

* **Gallery Preview:** A curated selection of 4-6 stunning photos from the gallery, arranged in a modern masonry grid.

* **Footer:** Links to all major sections, social media icons, and contact information.

### **Clubs**

* **Main Clubs Page:** A directory of all clubs under the STC. Each club should be represented by a card containing its logo, name, and a short one-sentence description.

* **Individual Club Pages:** Each club (CCIT, CMIT, Persec, PSIT, CSIT, Proteus, etc.) will have its own dedicated page with the following sections:

  * **Header:** Club logo and full name.

  * **About the Club:** A detailed description of the club's mission, activities, and goals.

  * **Team/Members:** Profiles of the club's leadership and key members (with photos).

  * **Events/Workshops:** A list of past and upcoming events organized by the club.

  * **Gallery:** A dedicated photo gallery for the club's activities.

  * **Contact/Social Media:** Links to the club's social media pages and contact person.

### **Gallery**

* **Modern & Interactive:** A full-page, filterable gallery.

  * **Filters:** Allow users to filter images by event (e.g., Anvesha 2024), club, or year.

  * **Layout:** A dynamic masonry grid that looks great on all screen sizes.

  * **Lightbox:** Clicking on an image opens it in a full-screen lightbox with options to navigate between images.

  * **High-Resolution:** Optimized for fast loading without compromising image quality.

### **Events**

* **Main Events Page:** A calendar or timeline view of all STC events.

  * **Past Events Archive:** A section for past events with links to their respective galleries and summaries.

  * **Anvesha Section:** A dedicated, prominent section for Anvesha, the annual science fest. This could have its own sub-page with more details, schedules, and registration links.

### **Updates and Announcements**

* A blog-style page with all official news, announcements, and updates from the STC, sorted chronologically.

### **Leadership & Governance**

* **Faculty-in-Charge (FIC) & Dean of Student Affairs (DOSA):**

  * A professional page with photos, names, and messages from the current FIC and DOSA.

* **STC Council:**

  * Profiles of the current STC secretaries and other council members (with photos, positions, and brief bios).

* **Past Secretaries:**

  * A dedicated page or section honoring past STC secretaries, with their names, tenures, and photos. This builds a sense of legacy and history.

### **About**

* **About the STC:** A detailed page explaining the history, mission, and structure of the Science and Technology Council at IISER TVM.

* **Contact Us:**

  * Contact form for general inquiries.

  * Official email address.

  * Links to social media profiles (LinkedIn, Instagram, etc.).

  * An embedded Google Maps view of the IISER TVM campus.

### **FAQs**

* An accordion-style FAQ section to answer common questions about the STC, its clubs, and events (e.g., "How can I join a club?", "When is Anvesha held?").

## 3. Content Checklist

To bring this website to life, the following content is required:

* **Logos:** High-resolution, transparent background (PNG/SVG) logos for the STC and all affiliated clubs.

* **Images:**

  * A large collection of high-quality photos for the gallery, homepage, and individual club pages.

  * Professional headshots for all members, secretaries, FIC, and DOSA.

* **Text Content:**

  * Written content for all "About" sections (STC and clubs).

  * Messages from the FIC and DOSA.

  * Detailed descriptions of all major events.

  * Content for the FAQs page.

* **Contact Information:**

  * Official email addresses and social media links.

* **Member Details:**

  * A comprehensive list of current and past STC secretaries and council members, including their names, positions, and tenures.

This blueprint provides a comprehensive guide for creating a website that is both functional and aesthetically pleasing.             animation: dotFlashing 1s infinite alternate;

            border-radius: 5px;
            background-color: #9880ff;
            color: #9880ff;
            animation: dotFlashing 1s infinite alternate;
            animation-delay: 1s;
        }
        @keyframes dotFlashing {
            0% { background-color: #9880ff; }
            50%, 100% { background-color: rgba(152, 128, 255, 0.2); }
        }
    </style>
</head>
<body class="bg-gray-900 text-white font-sans flex items-center justify-center min-h-screen">

    <!-- Main Chat Container -->
    <div class="w-full max-w-3xl h-[95vh] bg-gray-800 rounded-2xl shadow-2xl flex flex-col p-4 md:p-6">
        
        <!-- Header -->
        <header class="border-b border-gray-700 pb-4 mb-4">
            <h1 class="text-2xl font-bold text-center text-purple-400">AI Chatbot Portfolio</h1>
            <p id="status" class="text-center text-gray-400 text-sm mt-1">Loading model... (this might take a moment on first visit)</p>
        </header>

        <!-- Chat Box -->
        <div id="chat-box" class="flex-1 overflow-y-auto p-4 space-y-4 bg-gray-900/50 rounded-lg">
             <!-- Typing indicator will be added here -->
        </div>

        <!-- Predefined Prompts -->
        <div class="mt-4 pt-4 border-t border-gray-700">
            <p class="text-sm text-gray-400 mb-2 text-center">Or try one of these creative prompts:</p>
            <div id="prompt-buttons" class="flex flex-wrap justify-center gap-2">
                <button class="prompt-btn">Write a haiku about a robot dreaming.</button>
                <button class="prompt-btn">What if the moon was made of cheese?</button>
                <button class="prompt-btn">Describe the color blue to someone who can't see.</button>
                 <button class="prompt-btn">Explain quantum computing with a simple analogy.</button>
            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- Input Area -->
        <div id="input-area" class="mt-4 pt-4 flex items-center gap-3">
            <input id="user-input" type="text" placeholder="Type your message..." class="flex-1 bg-gray-700 border border-gray-600 rounded-lg py-3 px-4 focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-purple-500 transition duration-300 disabled:opacity-50" disabled>
            <button id="send-button" class="bg-purple-600 hover:bg-purple-500 text-white font-bold py-3 px-5 rounded-lg transition duration-300 disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed flex items-center justify-center">
                <i class="fas fa-paper-plane"></i>
            </button>
        </div>
    </div>

    <!-- JavaScript Logic -->
    <script type="module">
        // Import the pipeline function from the Transformers.js library
        import { pipeline } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@xenova/transformers/dist/transformers.min.js";

        // Get references to DOM elements
        const status = document.getElementById("status");
        const chatBox = document.getElementById("chat-box");
        const userInput = document.getElementById("user-input");
        const sendButton = document.getElementById("send-button");
        const promptButtonsContainer = document.getElementById("prompt-buttons");

        let generator; // This will hold the AI model pipeline

        /**
         * Creates and appends a styled chat message to the chat box.
         * @param {string} sender - Who sent the message ('You' or 'Bot').
         * @param {string} message - The content of the message.
         */
        function addChatMessage(sender, message) {
            const messageWrapper = document.createElement('div');
            messageWrapper.className = `flex ${sender === 'You' ? 'justify-end' : 'justify-start'}`;
            
            const messageElement = document.createElement("div");
            messageElement.className = `max-w-md md:max-w-lg p-3 rounded-2xl shadow-md`;
            
            if (sender === 'You') {
                messageElement.classList.add('bg-purple-700', 'text-white', 'rounded-br-none');
            } else {
                messageElement.classList.add('bg-gray-700', 'text-gray-200', 'rounded-bl-none');
            }
            
            messageElement.textContent = message;
            messageWrapper.appendChild(messageElement);
            chatBox.appendChild(messageWrapper);
            chatBox.scrollTop = chatBox.scrollHeight;
        }

        /**
         * Shows or hides the typing indicator.
         * @param {boolean} show - Whether to show the indicator.
         */
        function toggleTypingIndicator(show) {
            let indicator = document.getElementById('typing-indicator');
            if (show && !indicator) {
                indicator = document.createElement('div');
                indicator.id = 'typing-indicator';
                indicator.className = 'flex items-center space-x-2 justify-start';
                indicator.innerHTML = `
                    <div class="p-3 rounded-2xl bg-gray-700">
                        <div class="dot-flashing"></div>
                    </div>
                `;
                chatBox.appendChild(indicator);
                chatBox.scrollTop = chatBox.scrollHeight;
            } else if (!show && indicator) {
                indicator.remove();
            }
        }

        /**
         * Initializes the AI model pipeline.
         */
        async function initializeModel() {
            try {
                // Load the text-generation pipeline with a small, efficient model.
                generator = await pipeline("text-generation", "Xenova/distilgpt2");
                status.textContent = "Model loaded. Ready to chat!";
                
                userInput.disabled = false;
                sendButton.disabled = false;
                userInput.placeholder = "Ask me anything...";
                
                addChatMessage("Bot", "Hello! I'm an AI running locally in your browser. Ask me something or try a prompt below!");

            } catch (err) {
                status.textContent = "Error: Could not load the model.";
                console.error("Model loading error:", err);
                addChatMessage("Bot", "Sorry, I couldn't initialize. Please try refreshing the page.");
            }
        }

        /**
         * Handles sending a message to the bot and getting a response.
         */
        async function handleSendMessage() {
            const userText = userInput.value.trim();
            if (!userText || !generator) return;

            addChatMessage("You", userText);
            userInput.value = "";

            userInput.disabled = true;
            sendButton.disabled = true;
            toggleTypingIndicator(true);

            try {
                // Generate a response from the model
                const output = await generator(userText, {
                    max_new_tokens: 100,
                    temperature: 0.8,
                    repetition_penalty: 1.2,
                    no_repeat_ngram_size: 2,
                });

                const reply = output[0].generated_text.slice(userText.length).trim();
                addChatMessage("Bot", reply || "I'm not quite sure what to say to that.");

            } catch (err) {
                console.error("Generation error:", err);
                addChatMessage("Bot", "Apologies, I encountered an error while thinking.");
            } finally {
                toggleTypingIndicator(false);
                status.textContent = "Model loaded. Ready to chat!";
                userInput.disabled = false;
                sendButton.disabled = false;
                userInput.focus();
            }
        }

        // --- Event Listeners ---
        document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', initializeModel);
        sendButton.addEventListener('click', handleSendMessage);
        userInput.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
            if (event.key === 'Enter') {
                handleSendMessage();
            }
        });

        promptButtonsContainer.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
            if (event.target.classList.contains('prompt-btn')) {
                const promptText = event.target.textContent;
                userInput.value = promptText;
                handleSendMessage(); // Automatically send the prompt on click
            }
        });

        // Add styling to prompt buttons
        document.querySelectorAll('.prompt-btn').forEach(button => {
            button.className = 'px-4 py-2 bg-gray-700 hover:bg-gray-600 text-gray-300 rounded-lg text-sm transition duration-300 cursor-pointer';
        });
    </script>
</body>
</html>

            async sendMessage() {
                const messageText = this.messageInput.value.trim();
                if (!messageText) return;

                this.addMessage(messageText, 'user');
                this.messageInput.value = '';
                this.typingIndicator.style.display = 'flex';

                try {
                    const response = await this.getAIResponse(messageText);
                    this.addMessage(response, 'bot');
                } catch (error) {
                    this.addMessage('I apologize, but I encountered an error. Please try again.', 'bot');
                    console.error('Error:', error);
                }

                this.typingIndicator.style.display = 'none';
            }

            async getAIResponse(message) {
                const API_ENDPOINT = 'https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions';
                const API_KEY = '[REDACTED_GROQ_KEY]';

                try {
                    const response = await fetch(API_ENDPOINT, {
                        method: 'POST',
                        headers: {
                            'Content-Type': 'application/json',
                            'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`
                        },
                        body: JSON.stringify({
                            messages: [
                                {
                                    role: "system",
                                    content: this.defaultSystemPrompt
                                },
                                {
                                    role: "user",
                                    content: message
                                }
                            ],
                            model: "llama-3.3-70b-versatile",
                            temperature: 0.2,
                            seed: 10,
                            top_p: 0.9
                        })
                    });

                    if (!response.ok) {
                        throw new Error(`HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`);
                    }

                    const data = await response.json();
                    return data.choices[0].message.content;

                } catch (error) {
                    console.error('Error:', error);
                    throw error;
                }
            }

            addMessage(text, sender) {
                const messageDiv = document.createElement('div');
                messageDiv.classList.add('message', `${sender}-message`);

                if (sender === 'bot') {
                    const markdownDiv = document.createElement('div');
                    markdownDiv.classList.add('markdown-body');
                    markdownDiv.innerHTML = marked.parse(text);

                    messageDiv.querySelectorAll('pre code').forEach(hljs.highlightElement);
                } else {
                    messageDiv.textContent = text;
                }

                this.chatMessages.appendChild(messageDiv);
                this.chatMessages.scrollTop = this.chatMessages.scrollHeight;
            }
        }

    </script>

    import { pipeline } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@xenova/transformers/dist/transformers.min.js";

    let generator;

    async function init() {
      const status = document.getElementById("status");

    async function sendMessage() {
      const input = document.getElementById("user-input");

      const userText = input.value.trim();
      if (!userText) return;

      chatBox.innerHTML += `<div><b>You:</b> ${userText}</div>`;
      input.value = "";

      const status = document.getElementById("status");
      status.textContent = "Thinking...";

      try {
        const output = await generator(userText, {
          max_new_tokens: 50,
          temperature: 0.7,
        });

        const reply = output[0].generated_text;
        chatBox.innerHTML += `<div><b>Bot:</b> ${reply}</div>`;
      } catch (err) {
        chatBox.innerHTML += `<div><b>Error:</b> ${err.message}</div>`;
      }

      status.textContent = "";
      chatBox.scrollTop = chatBox.scrollHeight;
    }

    window.onload = init;
    window.sendMessage = sendMessage;

% Author: A fellow student (proficient in Python, learning MATLAB)
% Date: 20-Aug-2025
%
% This script solves the given problem in four parts.
% 1. Manual error calculation (explained in comments).
% 2. A MATLAB function to compute the error.
% 3. A log-log plot of step size 'h' vs. error.
% 4. Comments explaining the behavior of the error.
%

% Housekeeping commands, similar to clearing a console and closing plots.
clear;
clc;
close all;

%% Part 1: Manual Error Calculation

% The problem asks for the error in the forward difference approximation for
% f(x) = sin(x) at x0 = 1.2.
%
% The approximation formula is: f'(x0) ≈ [f(x0 + h) - f(x0)] / h
%
% 1.  **Find the True Derivative:**
%     The derivative of f(x) = sin(x) is f'(x) = cos(x).
%     So, the true value at x0 = 1.2 is f'(1.2) = cos(1.2).
%     Using a calculator, cos(1.2) ≈ 0.36235775.
%
% 2.  **Define the Approximation:**
%     The approximation is [sin(1.2 + h) - sin(1.2)] / h.
%
% 3.  **Define the Error:**
%     The error is the absolute difference between the true value and the
%     approximation.
%     Error(h) = |cos(1.2) - (sin(1.2 + h) - sin(1.2)) / h|
%
%     The error is a function of 'h'. For example, if we manually compute
%     for h = 0.01:
%     Approx ≈ (sin(1.21) - sin(1.2)) / 0.01 ≈ (0.935616 - 0.932039) / 0.01 ≈ 0.3577
%     Error ≈ |0.362358 - 0.3577| ≈ 0.004658
%
% The general formula for the error is what we derived in step 3.

%% Part 3: Plot h versus the Absolute Error

% NOTE: The function for Part 2 is defined at the end of this script.

fprintf('Generating plot for h vs. absolute error...\n');

% Define the point where we are evaluating the derivative
x0 = 1.2;

% Create a vector of h values. logspace is great for this, kind of like
% np.logspace in Python. We need to go to very small values to see the effect.
h_values = logspace(-16, 0, 200); % 200 points from 10^-16 to 10^0

% Pre-allocate an array for the errors. This is more efficient in MATLAB
% than appending to a list like in Python.
errors = zeros(size(h_values));

% Loop through each h and calculate the error using our function
for i = 1:length(h_values)
    errors(i) = computeForwardDiffError(h_values(i), x0);
end

% Create the log-log plot
figure; % This opens a new window for the plot
loglog(h_values, errors, 'b-o', 'LineWidth', 1.5, 'MarkerSize', 3);

% Add titles and labels to make the plot clear and professional
title('Error in Forward Difference vs. Step Size h');
xlabel('Step Size (h)');
ylabel('Absolute Error');
grid on;
legend('Absolute Error', 'Location', 'SouthEast');

fprintf('Plot generated successfully.\n');

%% Part 4: Observation and Explanation

% =========================================================================
%               OBSERVATION AND COMMENTS ON THE PLOT'S BEHAVIOR
% =========================================================================
%
% ### What's Happening in the Plot?
% The plot has a very distinct "V" shape.
%
% 1.  **Right Side (h from 1 down to ~10⁻⁸):** As we decrease the step size 'h',
%     the error steadily decreases. This is what we'd intuitively expect.
%     A smaller step size should give a better approximation. On the log-log
%     scale, this part is a straight line, indicating the error is
%     proportional to h (specifically, the error is O(h)).
%
% 2.  **Left Side (h smaller than ~10⁻⁸):** When we reduce 'h' drastically,
%     something weird happens. The error stops decreasing and actually
%     starts to increase again! This is counter-intuitive.
%
% ### Why Does This Happen? The Two-Error Trade-off
%
% This behavior is a classic example of the battle between two types of errors
% in numerical computing: **truncation error** and **round-off error**.
%
% #### 1. Truncation Error
% This error comes from the approximation method itself. We "truncated" a
% Taylor series to get the forward difference formula. This error is
% proportional to 'h'. So, as 'h' gets smaller, the truncation error gets
% smaller. This explains the right side of the "V".
%
% #### 2. Round-off Error
% This error comes from the computer's limitations. Computers use finite
% precision (floating-point numbers) to store values.
%
% When 'h' becomes extremely small:
%   - The term `x0 + h` becomes almost identical to `x0`.
%   - The subtraction `sin(x0 + h) - sin(x0)` is then a subtraction of two
%     nearly equal numbers. This leads to a massive loss of significant digits,
%     an effect called **catastrophic cancellation**.
%   - The result of the subtraction is a very small number that is mostly
%     noise (inaccuracy).
%   - We then divide this highly inaccurate small number by another tiny
%     number 'h', which magnifies the error enormously.
%
% This round-off error dominates for very small 'h', which explains why the
% error shoots back up on the left side of the "V".
%
% ### Conclusion 💡
% The optimal 'h' is at the bottom of the "V" (around 10⁻⁸ for standard
% double precision). At this point, the truncation and round-off errors are
% balanced. Making 'h' any smaller actually makes our derivative
% approximation *worse*, not better.
% =========================================================================


%% Part 2: Matlab Function to Compute Absolute Error

function absolute_error = computeForwardDiffError(h, x0)
    % Computes the absolute error of the forward difference approximation
    % for f(x) = sin(x) at a given point x0 and for a step size h.
    % It's good practice in MATLAB to have functions at the end of a script
    % or in their own separate .m file.

    % 1. Calculate the true value of the derivative f'(x) = cos(x)
    true_derivative = cos(x0);

    % 2. Calculate the forward difference approximation
    %    f'(x0) ≈ [f(x0+h) - f(x0)] / h
    approx_derivative = (sin(x0 + h) - sin(x0)) / h;

    % 3. Compute the absolute error
    absolute_error = abs(true_derivative - approx_derivative);

% MATLAB Program to Compute Machine Epsilon
%
% This script calculates the approximate value of machine epsilon (eps),
% which is the smallest positive floating-point number such that
% 1.0 + eps is not equal to 1.0.

fprintf('Starting calculation for machine epsilon...\n');

% 1. Initialize epsilon to 1.0. We will use double precision by default.
epsilon = 1.0;

% 2. Loop to find the machine epsilon.
% We check if (1.0 + epsilon/2.0) is still greater than 1.0.
% The loop continues as long as the computer can distinguish the sum from 1.
while (1.0 + (epsilon / 2.0)) > 1.0
    % If the condition is true, it means epsilon is not yet the smallest
    % possible value. So, we halve it and try again.
    epsilon = epsilon / 2.0;
end

% 3. Display the result.
% When the loop terminates, 'epsilon' holds the smallest value found.
fprintf('Calculated Machine Epsilon: %e\n', epsilon);

% 4. Compare with MATLAB's built-in function.
% The 'eps' command in MATLAB returns the machine epsilon for double precision.
% This is a good way to verify our result.
fprintf('MATLAB''s built-in value (eps): %e\n', eps);

These are the most important definitions in this part of linear algebra. Let's break them down carefully. The Core Definitions The text introduces three linked concepts. The names can be a bit confusing, so let's clarify them. While your book uses "characteristic," the term "eigen" (from German, meaning "own" or "proper") is far more common today. I'll use both. Characteristic Value (Eigenvalue), c : This is a special scalar . It's the factor by which a special vector is stretched or shrunk by the transformation T . Characteristic Vector (Eigenvector), α : This is a special non-zero vector . When T acts on it, the output T(α) is simply a scaled version of the original vector, cα . Crucial point : We insist that eigenvectors be non-zero . This is because T(0) = 0 for any linear transformation, so T(0) = c * 0 is true for any scalar c . Including the zero vector would make the concept useless, as every scalar would be an eigenvalue. Characteristic Space (Eigenspace) : For a specific eigenvalue c , the eigenspace is the set of all vectors α (including the zero vector) such that T(α) = cα . This collection forms a subspace of V . In this image, the blue vector α is an eigenvector of the transformation T . The transformation turns it into the red vector T(α) , which is just cα . It's on the same line through the origin. The Key Insight: From Tα = cα to a Null Space How do we actually find these values and vectors? Staring at T(α) = cα is not the most practical way. The book shows the crucial algebraic step that turns this into a problem we already know how to solve: finding a null space. Start with the defining equation: T(α) = cα Subtract cα from both sides: T(α) - cα = 0 Introduce the identity operator I (where I(α) = α ). This lets us factor out α : T(α) - cI(α) = 0 Factor out α : (T - cI)(α) = 0 This final equation, (T - cI)(α) = 0 , tells us everything. It says that any eigenvector α associated with the eigenvalue c is a vector in the null space of the operator (T - cI) . The eigenspace for c is precisely the null space of (T - cI) . The "Aha!" Moment: Using Determinants We are only interested in cases where we can find a non-zero eigenvector α . So, the question "For which scalars c does a non-zero eigenvector exist?" becomes: "For which scalars c is the null space of (T - cI) non-trivial (i.e., contains more than just the zero vector)?" We have a perfect tool for this! A linear operator (on a finite-dimensional space) has a non-trivial null space if and only if it is not invertible . And the test for invertibility is the determinant. An operator is invertible if its determinant is non-zero . An operator is not invertible if its determinant is zero . Therefore, to find the characteristic values (eigenvalues), we need to find the scalars c that make the operator (T - cI) not invertible . We do this by solving the equation: $$\det(T - cI) = 0$$ This is called the characteristic equation . Note on the Text: Your book has a significant typo at the end of the section. It says (T - cI) fails to be 1-to-1 "precisely when its determinant is different from 0." This is incorrect. It fails to be 1-to-1 precisely when its determinant IS equal to 0 . This is a critical distinction. General Way to Solve These Questions Goal: Given a matrix A representing T , find its eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Step 1: Find the Eigenvalues (c). Set up the characteristic equation: det(A - cI) = 0 . (Sometimes the variable λ is used instead of c ). Solve this equation for c . The solutions are your eigenvalues. Step 2: Find the Eigenvectors (α) for EACH eigenvalue. For each eigenvalue c you found, plug it back into the equation (A - cI)α = 0 . Solve this system of linear equations for α . This is just finding the null space of the matrix (A - cI) . The non-zero solution vectors are the eigenvectors for that c . The set of all solutions is the eigenspace. Sample Problem & Solution Problem: Let the operator T on R^2 be represented by the matrix A = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} . Find the characteristic values (eigenvalues) of T and the characteristic space (eigenspace) for each value. Solution: Step 1: Find the Eigenvalues We need to solve det(A - cI) = 0 . A - cI = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} - c\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 4-c & -1 \\ 2 & 1-c \end{bmatrix} \det(A - cI) = (4-c)(1-c) - (-1)(2) = 4 - 5c + c^2 + 2 = c^2 - 5c + 6 Set the determinant to zero: c^2 - 5c + 6 = 0 Factor the polynomial: (c - 2)(c - 3) = 0 The characteristic values are c_1 = 2 and c_2 = 3 . Step 2: Find the Eigenspaces Case 1: Find the eigenspace for c = 2. We need to solve (A - 2I)α = 0 . A - 2I = \begin{bmatrix} 4-2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1-2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix} The system is \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} .
This gives the equation 2x_1 - x_2 = 0 , or x_2 = 2x_1 .
The eigenvectors are any non-zero vectors of the form \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ 2x_1 \end{bmatrix} . A simple choice is \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} .
The characteristic space for c=2 is the set of all vectors k \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} for any scalar k . Case 2: Find the eigenspace for c = 3. We need to solve (A - 3I)α = 0 . A - 3I = \begin{bmatrix} 4-3 & -1 \\ 2 & 1-3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 \end{bmatrix} The system is \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} .
This gives the equation x_1 - x_2 = 0 , or x_1 = x_2 .
The eigenvectors are any non-zero vectors of the form \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_1 \end{bmatrix} . A simple choice is \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} .

Let's break down the mission statement for this chapter. The Core Idea: Making Transformations Simple Think of everything you've learned so far—vector spaces, bases, linear transformations, matrices—as building blocks. Now, we're going to use all those blocks for a single purpose: to understand a single linear operator T as deeply as possible. The main idea is this: A linear transformation T can be represented by many different matrices. It all depends on the basis you choose. Our goal is to find the best possible basis , where "best" means the basis that makes the matrix for T as simple as it can be. Intuition: Finding the "Best" Viewpoint Imagine you have a complicated 3D object, like a crystal. If you look at it from a random angle, its shadow on the wall might be a complex, messy shape. But, if you rotate the crystal to just the right orientation, its shadow might become a simple, clean shape like a hexagon. The linear transformation T is like that crystal. The basis is the "angle" from which we are looking. And the matrix [T]_B is the "shadow" it casts. We are looking for that special basis where the matrix representation is incredibly simple. What's the simplest possible matrix? As the text says, a diagonal matrix . $$D = \begin{bmatrix} c_1 & 0 & \dots & 0 \\ 0 & c_2 & \dots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \dots & c_n \end{bmatrix}$$ Why is this so simple? Because all the non-zero numbers are neatly arranged on the main diagonal. All other entries are zero. This makes computations (like finding powers of the matrix, its determinant, or its rank) incredibly easy. The Perfect Scenario: What a Diagonal Matrix Means The book gives the most important equation of this chapter right away. It says that having a diagonal matrix [T]_B = D for a basis B = {α_1, α_2, ..., α_n} is the same as saying: $$T(α_k) = c_k \cdot α_k \quad \text{for each basis vector } α_k$$ Let's unpack this. This equation means that for these very special basis vectors α_k , the transformation T does something remarkably simple: it just stretches or shrinks the vector α_k by a factor of c_k . The output T(α_k) points in the exact same (or opposite) direction as the input α_k . Example: Imagine T is a transformation in R^2 and we find a basis B = {α_1, α_2} such that T(α_1) = 3α_1 and T(α_2) = -2α_2 . In this basis, the matrix for T is: $$[T]_B = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$$ The transformation T stretches every vector in the direction of α_1 by a factor of 3 and flips and stretches every vector in the direction of α_2 by a factor of 2. For any other vector (which is a combination of α_1 and α_2 ), T acts on its components separately. This completely describes the "behavior" or the "action" of T in the simplest way possible. The vectors α_k are later called eigenvectors and the scalars c_k are called eigenvalues . This relationship is the key that unlocks the entire process. The Guiding Questions This introduction sets up the plot for the rest of the chapter by asking the key questions we need to answer: Is it always possible? Can every linear operator be represented by a diagonal matrix? (Hint: The answer is no.) Which operators work? If not all operators can be diagonalized, what properties must an operator have? How do we do it? If an operator can be diagonalized, how do we find that special basis? What if we fail? If we can't find a diagonal matrix, what's the next-best, "simplest" matrix we can find? (This is a teaser for a later topic, the Jordan Canonical Form). This section is all about motivation. It's telling you why you should care about the upcoming concepts. We are on a quest to find the "soul" of a linear transformation, and it starts by trying to make its matrix diagonal. Ready for the next section when you are! Products: Gemini Apps Why is this here? Based on the text in the abstract, the modeling approach is not a Neural Network (NN) . Instead, they are using a combination of metabolic network construction and graph algorithms . Here's a breakdown of the modeling process described: Network Construction (The Model Itself): The core of their model is a "lipid interaction network." This is essentially a graph. Nodes: The individual lipid species. Edges: The biochemical reactions that convert one lipid into another, catalyzed by specific enzymes.
The crucial part is that they build this network by integrating pre-existing biological knowledge from public databases (like KEGG, Reactome, etc.). This is a "knowledge-driven" approach, very different from a neural network that learns relationships from scratch. The Algorithm for Analysis: The abstract explicitly mentions they use " graph algorithms " to analyze this network. While the text cuts off, it specifies one type: an " enrichment graph algorithm ." What is an enrichment algorithm? In bioinformatics, enrichment analysis is a statistical method used to determine if a pre-defined set of genes, proteins, or in this case, lipids, are over-represented (i.e., "enriched") in a larger list of items showing significant change. In simple terms, their process is: Build a Map: Create a detailed map (a network/graph) of all known lipid reactions. Overlay Data: Take the user's experimental data (which lipids have changed in their experiment) and highlight them on the map. Find Hotspots: Use a statistical algorithm (the "enrichment graph algorithm") to find which pathways or regions on the map have a surprisingly high number of highlighted lipids. These "hotspots" point to the likely source of the problem, such as a specific dysregulated enzyme. Why this is not a Neural Network: Interpretability vs. Black Box: The graph network approach is highly interpretable. The results directly point to specific, known metabolic pathways. Neural networks are often referred to as "black boxes" because while they can be very powerful for prediction, it's often difficult to understand why they made a certain decision. The authors' goal is to find "mechanistic alterations," so interpretability is key. Knowledge-Driven vs. Data-Driven: This method starts with a framework of known biological rules. An NN would typically be trained on vast amounts of input data (e.g., lipid levels) and output data (e.g., disease status) to learn the patterns itself, without being explicitly given the map of metabolic pathways. In summary, they are using a knowledge-based graph model combined with statistical enrichment algorithms to make biological sense of complex lipidomics data. Products: Gemini Apps Why is this here? Core Research Problem Lipidomics data is complex: Modern techniques can measure thousands of different types of lipids in a biological sample. The challenge is interpretation: While we can see which lipids go up or down, it's difficult to understand why . The goal is to connect these changes to specific biological processes, like the malfunctioning of a particular enzyme, which could be a driver of a disease. 2. Proposed Solution: LINEX The authors have developed a computational framework and software tool named LINEX (Lipid Network Explorer) to address this problem. The key features of LINEX described in the abstract are: Network-based approach: It doesn't look at lipids in isolation. Instead, it constructs "lipid interaction networks." Integration of public data: LINEX builds these networks by pulling information about known lipid metabolic reactions from public scientific databases. Context-specific analysis: The networks it generates are tailored to the specific biological context being studied (e.g., a specific cell type or disease). Interpretation tools: The paper mentions the development of an "enrichment graph" and other analysis methods to help researchers interpret these complex networks and pinpoint the most significant alterations. 3. Key Concepts and Terminology Lipidomics: The large-scale study of lipids in a biological system. It's a sub-field of metabolomics. Lipid Network: A map showing how different lipid molecules are connected through biochemical reactions (e.g., Lipid A is converted to Lipid B by Enzyme 1). Analyzing this network can reveal bottlenecks or overactive pathways. Moiety Analysis: A "moiety" is a distinct part of a molecule. For lipids, this could mean analyzing the head groups or the attached fatty acid chains separately. This allows for a more detailed view of structural changes across many lipid classes. Enzymatic Dysregulation: The abnormal functioning (either over-activity or under-activity) of enzymes. Since enzymes control the production and breakdown of lipids, their dysregulation directly impacts lipid composition. Mechanistic Alterations: Changes in the fundamental biological machinery. The goal of the paper is to move from just observing changes in lipid levels to understanding the mechanism causing them. 4. Authors and Institutions Corresponding Author: Josch K. I was unable to access the Google Share link you provided, but I found the paper on arXiv. Here is a line-by-line explanation of the paper: Core Idea: The paper introduces a new technique called "persona vectors" to identify and control specific personality traits in large language models (LLMs). These vectors are essentially directions in the model's internal "activation space" that correspond to traits like being evil, sycophantic (overly agreeable), or prone to hallucination. Key Findings and Applications: Monitoring: By tracking how a model's activations align with these persona vectors, researchers can monitor its personality in real-time. This is useful for detecting undesirable changes in behavior after the model has been deployed. Prediction and Control: The paper shows that changes in a model's personality during fine-tuning are strongly correlated with shifts along the corresponding persona vectors. This allows researchers to predict how a model's personality will change and to intervene to prevent or mitigate these changes. Data Filtering: Persona vectors can be used to identify and flag training data that is likely to induce undesirable personality traits in a model. This can be done at both the dataset and individual sample level. Automated Process: The method for extracting persona vectors is automated and only requires a natural-language description of the personality trait of interest. How it Works (in simplified terms): Define a Trait: The process starts by defining a personality trait, such as "evil." Generate Contrasting Examples: The researchers then use the LLM to generate examples of text that are either very high or very low in that trait. For example, they would generate text that is very "evil" and text that is very "not evil." Identify the "Persona Vector": By comparing the model's internal activations when generating these contrasting examples, the researchers can identify the "persona vector" that corresponds to the "evil" trait. Control the Trait: Once the persona vector is identified, it can be used to "steer" the model's behavior. For example, by adding the "evil" vector to the model's activations, they can make the model behave more maliciously. Conversely, by subtracting the vector, they can make it less malicious. Implications: This research has significant implications for the safety and alignment of AI systems. By providing a way to monitor and control the personality of LLMs, persona vectors could help to prevent these models from developing harmful or undesirable behaviors. This is a crucial step towards building more reliable and trustworthy AI. In essence, this paper provides a powerful new tool for understanding and controlling the inner workings of LLMs. It's a significant advance in the field of AI safety and alignment. class Solution:
    # @param A: list of integers representing building positions
    # @param B: list of integers representing router positions
    # @return an integer representing the minimum required radius
    def findRadius(self, A, B):
        # Sort both lists to enable the two-pointer approach
        A.sort()
        B.sort()

        num_buildings = len(A)
        num_routers = len(B)

        # Edge case: If there are no buildings, no radius is needed.
        if num_buildings == 0:
            return 0
        
        # According to constraints, B is never empty.
        # This check is for robustness.
        if num_routers == 0:
            return float('inf') 

        max_radius = 0
        router_idx = 0  # Pointer for the router list B

        # Iterate through each building to find its minimum distance to a router
        for building_pos in A:
            
            # Advance the router pointer. This efficiently finds the two routers 
            # that "bracket" the current building's position.
            while router_idx < num_routers - 1 and B[router_idx + 1] <= building_pos:
                router_idx += 1
            
            # The closest router must be one of the two bracketing routers.
            # 1. Distance to the router at or to the left of the building
            dist_left = abs(building_pos - B[router_idx])
            
            min_dist_for_building = dist_left

            # 2. If a router exists to the right, check its distance as well
            if router_idx + 1 < num_routers:
                dist_right = abs(building_pos - B[router_idx + 1])
                min_dist_for_building = min(dist_left, dist_right)
            
            # The final radius must be large enough for the "worst-case" building
            max_radius = max(max_radius, min_dist_for_building)
            
        return max_radius Products: Gemini Apps Why is this here? This activity was saved to your Google Account because the following settings were on: Gemini Apps Activity. You can control these settings here .

class Solution:
    """
    Solves the Wi-Fi Router Installation problem.
    """
    def solve(self, A, B):
        """
        Calculates the minimum coverage radius for routers to cover all buildings.

        Args:
            A (list of int): Positions of buildings.
            B (list of int): Positions of routers.

        Returns:
            int: The minimum required radius.
        """
        # Sort both buildings and routers for the two-pointer approach
        A.sort()
        B.sort()

        num_buildings = len(A)
        num_routers = len(B)

        # If there are no buildings, no radius is needed
        if num_buildings == 0:
            return 0
        
        # Constraints state B is not empty, but this is good practice
        if num_routers == 0:
            return float('inf') 

        max_radius = 0
        router_idx = 0  # Pointer for the router array B

        # Iterate through each building
        for i in range(num_buildings):
            building_pos = A[i]

            # Advance router_idx to find routers that "bracket" the building
            # This brings router_idx to the last router that is <= building_pos
            while router_idx < num_routers - 1 and B[router_idx + 1] <= building_pos:
                router_idx += 1
            
            # The closest router is one of the two bracketing routers.
            # Calculate distance to the router on the left (or at the same position)
            dist_left = abs(building_pos - B[router_idx])
            
            min_dist_for_building = dist_left

            # If there's a router to the right, consider it as well
            if router_idx + 1 < num_routers:
                dist_right = abs(building_pos - B[router_idx + 1])
                min_dist_for_building = min(dist_left, dist_right)
            
            # The required radius must be at least the maximum of these minimum distances
            max_radius = max(max_radius, min_dist_for_building)
            
        return max_radius C++ #include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>

class Solution {
public:
    /**
     * @param A: A list of integers representing building positions.
     * @param B: A list of integers representing router positions.
     * @return: An integer representing the minimum required radius.
     */
    int solve(std::vector<int> &A, std::vector<int> &B) {
        // Sort both vectors for the two-pointer approach
        std::sort(A.begin(), A.end());
        std::sort(B.begin(), B.end());

        int num_buildings = A.size();
        int num_routers = B.size();

        if (num_buildings == 0) {
            return 0;
        }
        
        // Constraints state B is not empty
        if (num_routers == 0) {
            return -1; // Or throw an exception for an impossible case
        }

        int max_radius = 0;
        int router_idx = 0; // Pointer for the router vector B

        for (int i = 0; i < num_buildings; ++i) {
            int building_pos = A[i];

            // Advance router_idx to find bracketing routers
            while (router_idx < num_routers - 1 && B[router_idx + 1] <= building_pos) {
                router_idx++;
            }

            // Calculate distance to the router on the left (or at the same position)
            int dist_left = std::abs(building_pos - B[router_idx]);
            int min_dist_for_building = dist_left;

            // If there's a router to the right, consider its distance
            if (router_idx + 1 < num_routers) {
                int dist_right = std::abs(building_pos - B[router_idx + 1]);
                min_dist_for_building = std::min(dist_left, dist_right);
            }

            // Update the overall maximum radius needed
            max_radius = std::max(max_radius, min_dist_for_building);
        }

        return max_radius;
    }
}; Java import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.lang.Math;

public class Solution {
    /**
     * Calculates the minimum coverage radius for routers to cover all buildings.
     * @param A An ArrayList of integers representing building positions.
     * @param B An ArrayList of integers representing router positions.
     * @return An integer denoting the minimum coverage radius.
     */
    public int solve(ArrayList<Integer> A, ArrayList<Integer> B) {
        // Sort both lists for the two-pointer approach
        Collections.sort(A);
        Collections.sort(B);

        int numBuildings = A.size();
        int numRouters = B.size();

        if (numBuildings == 0) {
            return 0;
        }

        // Constraints state B is not empty
        if (numRouters == 0) {
            return Integer.MAX_VALUE; // Impossible case
        }

        int maxRadius = 0;
        int routerIdx = 0; // Pointer for the router list B

        for (int i = 0; i < numBuildings; i++) {
            int buildingPos = A.get(i);

            // Advance routerIdx to find bracketing routers
            while (routerIdx < numRouters - 1 && B.get(routerIdx + 1) <= buildingPos) {
                routerIdx++;
            }

            // Calculate distance to the router on the left (or at the same position)
            int distLeft = Math.abs(buildingPos - B.get(routerIdx));
            int minDistForBuilding = distLeft;

            // If there's a router to the right, consider its distance
            if (routerIdx + 1 < numRouters) {
                int distRight = Math.abs(buildingPos - B.get(routerIdx + 1));
                minDistForBuilding = Math.min(distLeft, distRight);
            }
            
            // Update the overall maximum radius needed
            maxRadius = Math.max(maxRadius, minDistForBuilding);
        }

        return maxRadius;
    }
} Products: Gemini Apps Why is this here? This activity was saved to your Google Account because the following settings were on: Gemini Apps Activity. You can control these settings here .
